name: Evening premium - Cutting Board Gel

explanation.reason: Evening hours convert materially better for this product. Paying a premium only in those hours buys the traffic that converts without raising the bid around the clock.

notes: One window covers ONE day, numbered 0 for Sunday through 6 for Saturday, so Mon-Fri is five windows. Times are HH:MM in 24-hour form, to the minute. Windows may not overlap.

Adjustments are percentages; there is no absolute adjustment. An increase is capped at 100% - a window can at most double the bid you set yourself - and a decrease at 99%, because 100% is not a bid, it is a pause.
Every adjustment is computed from your baseline bid rather than the live bid, so a raise cannot land on top of a raise.

lead_minutes shifts both edges of every window EARLIER, because Amazon propagates a bid change with a delay and writing at the exact boundary loses the edge of the window every day. Default 20, maximum 60.
This is a RECONCILER, not a scheduler. Every run asks 'given the time now, what should this bid be?' and corrects drift.
A missed restore in a scheduler model means paying the premium 24h/day until someone notices. Reconciling makes that self-healing.
Dayparting stacks with placement modifiers and Amazon dynamic bidding. Check the compounded bid.
Dayparting is on the Professional plan. campaign_ids takes Amazon campaign IDs, and a campaign can belong to only one dayparting schedule - two schedules would fight over the same bids every hour.
